section_summary: The section opens with correspondence about minimum export prices for Japanese binoculars and a Dutch complaint that Japanese enamelware was being offered at unusually low prices. It then contains a U.S. mission despatch forwarding Japanese Foreign Office studies of the 1930–34 standard of living. Most of the section is the 1947 study and the opening pages of its statistical annex.

subfiles.title: Letter protesting floor prices for Japanese binoculars
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sanders forwards his agent's complaint that a minimum export price blocks a cheaper binocular offer.
subfiles.summary: Requests investigation of the export price restriction and protection for suppliers who disclose their names.

subfiles.title: Letter on 7 × 50 binocular pricing
subfiles.about: Breen reports that Boeki Cho will not validate a $16.50 binocular contract because it requires at least $21.
subfiles.summary: Breen suspects larger manufacturers influenced the floor price, while acknowledging that this is his unverified opinion.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of complaint about binocular export prices
subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges Sanders's complaint about Japanese binocular floor prices.
subfiles.summary: Gay says occupation authorities seek export returns without encouraging monopolies and awaits their reply.

subfiles.title: Complaint concerning Japanese enamelware prices
subfiles.about: Jobsis alleges that Japanese enamelware offers undercut European prices and may constitute dumping.
subfiles.summary: Transmits comparative prices and a Japanese quotation for consideration under Far Eastern Commission policy.

subfiles.title: Comparison of European and Japanese enamelware prices
subfiles.about: Tables compare European association prices with Japanese offers for numerous enamelware articles.
subfiles.summary: The comparison lists sizes, units, prices, and percentage differences for kettles, bowls, basins, mugs, pots, and other goods. It identifies Osaka firms as the source of the Japanese prices.

subfiles.title: Enamelled wares export price quotation
subfiles.about: A Japanese export price list quotes enamelware and glass tumblers in U.S. dollars.
subfiles.summary: The list specifies article sizes, prices, packing, and f.o.b. Japanese port terms.

subfiles.title: Reply to Jobsis on enamelware price complaint
subfiles.about: Gay reports forwarding the enamelware complaint for review in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Returns the requested price list and promises a further reply after receiving a report.

subfiles.title: Instruction to investigate enamelware pricing complaint
subfiles.to: Office of the Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The Department asks occupation officials to investigate the Dutch enamelware complaint.
subfiles.summary: Requests a complete report and asks that Friele be informed.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese enamelware export prices
subfiles.about: Gay relays occupation officials' response to the allegation that Japanese enamelware is dumped abroad.
subfiles.summary: Officials cite quality differences, higher freight costs, buyer complaints, and Asian competition. Gay expects the new yen exchange rate to raise Japanese export prices.

subfiles.title: Forwarding studies of the Japanese standard of living
subfiles.about: The mission forwards two Japanese Foreign Office studies of the standard of living.
subfiles.summary: The despatch questions the later study's argument against the 1930–34 baseline and summarizes its projections for national income, industry, exports, and shipping.

subfiles.title: Report on Japan's Standard of Living, 1930–1934
subfiles.from: Provisional Committee on the 1930–34 Standard of Living, Japanese Foreign Office
subfiles.about: The report reconstructs Japan's 1930–34 population, economic activity, consumption, and standard of living.
subfiles.summary: It analyzes employment shifts toward industry, production, foreign trade, national income, household spending, and public services. It compares the 1930–34 baseline with other Japanese years and with selected countries, drawing on national income and living-standard measures.

subfiles.title: Annex to the Report on Japan's Standard of Living, 1930–1934
subfiles.from: Provisional Committee on the 1930–34 Standard of Living, Japanese Foreign Office
subfiles.about: The annex supplies statistical tables and charts supporting the standard-of-living report.
subfiles.summary: Pages in this section contain the contents list and initial tables on population, employment, industrial output, material supply and demand, and production values. The annex continues beyond page 65; intervening pages with no readable OCR remain part of it.
